answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a stake bond plus work-independence checks. To open a seat an agent locks collateral, and each identity must hold its own bond, so splitting into a grove of lookalikes multiplies cost instead of dividing it. If two puppets submit the same pigment of work, a correlation check flags both and burns the stake. Faking a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand bonds, and the horizon for any payoff is long enough that mass registration stays unprofitable.
